author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The global AI investment boom has become large enough to influence economic conditions and deserves closer financial-stability scrutiny, Bank for International Settlements chief Pablo Hernández de Cos said Thursday.

The BIS estimates that the five largest technology companies will invest more than $1 trillion in AI across 2025 and 2026. Industry projections cited by the central-bank organization put global AI investment at about $500 billion now and as much as $4 trillion by 2030.

Hernández de Cos said high valuations, concentrated markets and less transparent financing could create vulnerabilities if corporate profits fail to meet expectations. A growing share of AI infrastructure spending is being financed with debt and private credit instead of current earnings, increasing links between technology investment and financial markets.

The warning was not a forecast of a crash. The BIS chief also cited studies finding productivity gains of 10% to 65% in particular tasks, including coding and professional writing. For investors and policymakers, the central issue is whether those task-level gains spread across the economy quickly enough to justify the scale and financing cost of current spending.
dek: Pablo Hernández de Cos pointed to concentrated valuations and increasingly opaque debt financing while acknowledging AI’s productivity potential.
headline: BIS chief warns AI investment boom is creating financial-stability risks
